nodes.title: Round d38, the cap as built and judged: one more wording before the answer is told, no fifth hearing of a question on her own, two returns excepted; kept on the pair run d38a
After help at an asked worked step the step stays the open question and the child's answer is read against the step's own key (a fault live since 2026-11-18, fixed in round d38; kept on the pair run)
A walk change is tested by driven walks of the paths the offline matrix cannot reach, each read by check-run's whole gated list, before any paid run
The rule-based children answer only the question the walk holds open, so a path the walk wrongly closes is never run: every judged run before d38a shows no child answering a step after help

Pair run d38a: 8 lessons (c4-maths-ch01-t02, c6-maths-ch06-t01) on round d38's walk at 3f2e3e15a, two judges against director37: keep the cap, keep the step read after help; no question heard more than four times; 0 wrong marks

Round d38 offline: 36 lessons before and after: most hearings of one question 8 → 4; told answers 14 → 12, told steps 15 → 13, help turns 347 → 358, invitation endings 85 → 92; 197 teacher rows in 9 lessons change by the step read alone

Round d38: three independent reads (10 of the changed lessons) and three predicate reviews before the pair run: one walk fault and five script rows from the reads; ten driven-path faults from the reviews; the step read found sound on 25 driven paths
Taking an asked step's item off the table once she has helped at it (round d30, 045 P3): a right answer after help was asked again, for eight days in production, and no run could show it
Trusting the offline matrix as the test of a walk change: the cap's matrix read 0 on every gated check while hand-driven paths broke three earlier checks and misgraded a right answer
The order's C2: after her reply to a side-topic, the short ask in place of the question: two earlier judged rounds had taken exactly that out
Ruling a new rule from one driven walk without re-reading the judged rules it touches: four rulings of round d38 taken back within the hour
Telling the original card's answer straight after a follow-up card answered right, to avoid a fifth hearing: "Sahi jawab, kyunki … Nahi, kyunki 3 tukde barabar nahi …"
Putting a reader's board finding on the script list from the card's board alone: the screen as held was split and the sentence was true
A builder's report named a commit that does not exist; and a fix was described as verified on the matrix before the matrix was run

md.decisions:
- `dc-r8-d38-the-cap` (2026-11-26; part of `dc-r8-director37` item 3, which it carries out and corrects): the cap as built (`docs/patches/to-brain/055-director37-the-cap.md`, section "As built"). Where she would tell an answer at a question heard four times while a help wording of it is unsaid, she says that wording once, ending on an invitation, and tells at the next miss; at four hearings she does not say the question again on her own in any form; a fifth hearing is allowed once coming back from a side-topic (with one new wording) and once coming back from a remediation's follow-up card; a child who only says "haan" is told where help was said at that question before and helped once where it never was; a named wrong answer's own reason still comes before the told answer (order 054 C3). The order's C2 (the short ask after a side-topic reply) was dropped as wrong; S1 to S3 were not built and are carried. **Why:** director37's judges found the answer told with an easier wording unsaid in four lessons and one step heard eight times; on the pair run (`ms-r8-d38-pair`) both judges say keep: no question heard more than four times in eight lessons, and the told answer of director37's c6-maths-ch06-t01 steering 22 became the child's own answer. **Reverses if** a judge hears the one-more-wording turn as the wait going on (then the wording is said with the told answer); or hears a child who lost the question at a return (then the re-ask comes at the third hearing and the cap goes to five); or, for the three turns no run has reached (the told answer after a bare "haan" that follows the one-more-wording turn; after "let me try", the go-ahead and a bare "haan"; the way back from a follow-up card at four hearings), hears the child's try taken away (then the short ask or the question stands there once).
- `dc-r8-d38-step-read-after-help` (2026-11-26): after ANY help turn at an asked worked step, whatever that turn ends on, the step is still the open question and the child's next line is read against the step's own key exactly as straight after its ask (`stepOnTable`, `server/director/state.js`, commit 252a5a94f). **Why:** since commit 89dd33037 (round d30, 2026-11-18) the walk took the step's item off the table once she had helped, so a right answer was asked again (release 63's tree: "pata nahi", help, "5", the step asked again), and under the cap it would have been answered "Nahi, yeh nahi hai" (`rj-r8-step-answer-unread-after-help`). An independent review drove 25 step paths and found no misgrade and never another step's key; on the pair run both judges say keep (c4 offtopic 27 and c6 offtopic 17 confirmed straight after help; no right answer asked again, no wrong one confirmed). **Reverses if** a child's side-topic or request after help at a step is ever graded as a wrong answer, or a line is graded against another step's key: then the item goes back on the table only for a line the reader reads as an answer.
- `dc-r8-driven-walks-through-the-whole-gate` (2026-11-26): every walk round keeps a test of its own kind of `tests/r8-d38-055gate.test.mjs`: real walks through the director with the stub held for the whole walk, at a card and at an asked step, down every path the change opens that the four rule-based children do not take, each walk read by `check-run`'s WHOLE gated list with an empty expected list; and an independent reviewer drives further paths by hand before the paid run. **Why:** the cap's first offline matrix read 0 on every gated check while hand-driven paths broke three earlier checks and, later, showed a right answer called wrong (`rj-r8-clean-matrix-broken-driven-paths`); three reviews in a row each found faults only on driven paths. **Reverses if** two walk rounds running pass their first independent review with no driven-path finding: then the reviewer's hand-driven pass is dropped and the test alone stays.
- `dc-r8-harness-child-answers-after-help` (2026-11-26): what earlier runs measured is restated: in every judged run up to director37 the rule-based children said their next scripted line, not an answer, after help at an asked worked step, because the walk held no question open there. No run before the pair run d38a shows a child answering a step after help; from the first such moment the offtopic and stuck lessons of d38 take paths no earlier run has (197 teacher rows in 9 of 36 offline lessons). Comparisons of those lessons with director37 or earlier are of different paths. The harness list gains: a check that after every help turn at a step or a card the child's next line is an answer to it in at least one child of each topic. **Reverses if** the harness children are replaced by ones that answer from the transcript, not from the walk's open item.
md.measurements:
- `ms-r8-d38-pair` (2026-11-26): n = 8 lessons: c4-maths-ch01-t02 (staged) and c6-maths-ch06-t01 (live) by four rule-based children each, Director only, on `main/d38` at 3f2e3e15a (release 63's scripts word for word; round d38's walk). 698 model calls, about $0.50, 06:42 to 06:54 UTC, one part. `check-run` on the run: exit 0, every gated predicate 0. Two Opus judges at high effort, one topic each, by hand, against their topic's director37 report, with a cause sheet of two causes. **c6-maths-ch06-t01:** passes every gate line (150 of 150 beats, 108 of 108 verdicts over keyed answers, 0 contradictions, 0 unsaid boards, 0 wrong marks, 0 false keys); listening 4, worked example 4, class level 4, screen and speech 4.5, register 3.5, promises 4.5 → 4 ("Cricket wali baat maine likh li hai.", the walk's old fallback where the script has no kept form). **c4-maths-ch01-t02:** the walk passes every line (150 of 150, 95 of 95, 0 wrong marks); the judge counts 4 contradictions, all one script row (the cake card's board has no tester under words that point at one; the same rows in director37 were counted 0 by that judge); listening 3.5 → 4, register 3.5. **The cap:** no question heard more than four times in any lesson (director37: eight, c4 offtopic 22 to 46); two one-more-wording turns (c6 steering 22, c6 offtopic 34), each followed by the child's right answer where director37 told the answer at one of them; told answers and steps 4 in c4 (none by the cap; director37 one), 2 in c6 (director37 three). In c4 no question reached the cap. **The step read after help:** right answers straight after help confirmed at c4 offtopic 27 and c6 offtopic 17; every answer at a worked step on the new paths marked rightly. **Not reached by any child:** the three turns named in `dc-r8-d38-the-cap`'s reversal. Reports and cause sheet: `docs/design/round7/judgements/d38-pair-2026-11-26/`; main's reading in order 055, "Measured".
- `ms-r8-d38-dry-counts` (2026-11-26): the offline matrix (9 topics by 4 rule-based children, no model), release 63's tree (`d37/i/dry1`) against round d38's closed build (`d38/s2/dry1`, commit 3f2e3e15a; `check-run` exit 0, every gated predicate 0). Rows 2752 → 2748; turns over 60 words 217 → 218; check-in endings 132 → 130; invitation endings 85 → 92; told answers 14 → 12; told steps 15 → 13; help turns 347 → 358; most hearings of one question 8 → 4; questions heard four or more times 33 → 37. By cause: the cap alone (`d38/a4/dry1` against release 63) changed 73 teacher rows in 4 lessons (3 one-more-wording turns on a miss, 2 at a return, 1 at a wait, 67 shifted; most hearings 8 → 6); the step read after help alone (`d38/q/dry1` against `d38/p/dry1`) changed 197 teacher rows in 9 lessons, each from the child's first line after help at an asked step; the way back before a parked topic's return changed 3 rows (stuck c6-maths-ch06-t01 68 to 72). Method: `counts.mjs` over the matrix; rows compared word for word by the builders and spot-read by main.
- `ms-r8-d38-reads-and-reviews` (2026-11-26): before the pair run the round was read and reviewed by agents that did not build it (Opus, high effort). **Reads (as heard):** read 1, the cap's 6 changed turns in 4 lessons: better as heard, one A (a script wording that names a lower road over a one-road board). Read 2, two readers, the 9 lessons the step read changed, each whole from its first changed row (207 teacher turns): the new path better in 6, the same in 2, slightly worse in 1; every step and card answer marked rightly; 1 walk fault (a parked side-topic's return said before the way back to a card: fixed, `returnBeforeWayBack`), 5 script rows, and 1 finding that was the reader's misreading (a caption read against the card's board when the screen as held was split: the judge and the held record say the caption is true). **Reviews (checks and driven walks):** three passes by one reviewer; verdict NO each time; 3, then 3, then 4 faults, every one on a hand-driven path the offline matrix does not reach, none a misgrade; the step read (`stepOnTable`) driven down 25 paths in 4 scripts with no wrong mark. Reports: scratch `d38/wr1.md`, `wr2a.md`, `wr2b.md`, `pr1.md`, `pr2.md`, `pr3.md`.
md.rejected:
- `rj-r8-step-answer-unread-after-help` (2026-11-26): **tried** (round d30, commit 89dd33037) keeping help at an asked worked step "at the step" by a path that copied an item the walk had already taken off the table. **What broke:** after help at a step the child's line was read as nothing: a right answer was asked again (live from about 2026-11-18 to release 63), and with the cap it became "Nahi, yeh nahi hai … yaani 5" to a child who said 5. No judged run showed it in eight runs, because the rule-based children answer only the item the walk holds open and so never answered there. Found only when a test drove the path by hand through the whole gate.
- `rj-r8-clean-matrix-broken-driven-paths` (2026-11-26): **tried** closing a walk change on the offline matrix of the four rule-based children with every gated check at 0. **What broke:** the first independent review drove paths the children never take (the one-more-wording turn followed by each kind of child line) and three earlier gated checks flagged; a test of those paths then showed a right answer called wrong. The matrix exercises what the children say, not what the change opens.
- `rj-r8-short-ask-after-a-side-topic` (2026-11-26): **tried** (order 055 C2, written by main from one sentence of a judgement) "Ab phir se socho, jawab kya hoga?" as the way back to an open question after a side-topic. **What broke:** nothing ran: the builder would not exempt `shortAskNoAnswer` and `shortAskKind`, which hold two earlier rounds' finding that a child who has just talked about cricket does not know which question is meant. The same mistake twice more in the round: an invitation after a side-topic (`inviteAfterPark`), and the short ask after a remediation's follow-up card.
- `rj-r8-ruling-from-one-walk` (2026-11-26): **tried** ruling on a builder's stop from the one walk in front of main. **What broke:** four rulings were withdrawn within an hour each, every time because an existing gated check or test held a judged rule main had not re-read: one more wording at every wait (against main's own ruling that a bare "haan" asks for no wording; an order-054 test caught it); no remediation at the cap (`skillRemediation`); the told answer on the way back from a follow-up card (the walk read "Sahi jawab … Nahi, kyunki …"); the told answer in place of a named wrong answer's own reason (`capBeforeOwnReason`). Each cost a builder cycle. The checks were right every time: a clash with a gated check is first read as the check holding a rule.
- `rj-r8-told-answer-after-a-follow-up` (2026-11-26): **tried** (RULING-A10 T1) at a question heard four times: after its remediation's follow-up card, the follow-up's verdict and then the original card's told answer. **What broke:** as heard on the first driven walk, a right verdict ran straight into the yes-or-no card's "Nahi, kyunki …" about a question three turns old and never named. Built and undone the same morning; the way back is the question, as it always was.
- `rj-r8-readers-finding-not-checked-against-the-held-screen` (2026-11-26): **tried** filing a reader's A (a caption speaking of a line with four lengths over a plain rectangle) as a blocking script row. **What broke:** the pair run's judge read the row's `held` record: the screen was split, the rectangle beside the unrolled line with the four lengths, and the caption was true. The row was taken off the list. A finding about a board is checked against `held.layout`, not `board`, before it is ruled on.
- `rj-r8-builder-reports-a-hash-from-memory` (2026-11-26): **tried** taking commit hashes and "verified" from a builder's final message. **What broke:** one report named a hash that is not in the repository (the commit existed under another hash), and one commit message said "verified on the matrix" before the matrix had run (it did pass afterwards). Briefs now say: hashes from `git log`, never from memory; main reads `git log` itself.
